A.explanation: A charm quark is a fundamental particle in the quark family with no internal structure.

B.explanation: An electron is a fundamental lepton and is not made up of smaller particles.

C.explanation: A neutrino is a fundamental lepton and is not made up of smaller particles.

D.explanation: A neutron is a hadron made of three quarks, $u + d + d$, so it has internal structure and is not fundamental.

hints: Notice the word not - three of the listed particles have no internal structure and one is composite.
Recall the two families of fundamental particles in the Standard Model: the six quarks and the six leptons, which include the electron and neutrino.
Recall what the neutron is made of in the quark model and whether a particle made of $u$ and $d$ quarks can be fundamental.
walkthrough: Identify the test: a fundamental particle has no internal structure, while a composite particle is made of smaller particles.
Recall that quarks, including up, down, strange, charm, top and bottom, are fundamental particles.
Recall that leptons, including the electron and the electron-neutrino, are also fundamental particles.
Recall the quark structure of the neutron as a baryon made of three quarks: one up quark and two down quarks.
Since the neutron is made of quarks it is composite, not fundamental. This is option D.
